messages.subject: RAM requirements for prediction
parts:
Dear Juergen,

I have a question about prediction function of multi-species occupancy model. I used raster layers for species occupancy prediction. The whole size of my raster layers were about 30Gb. In the beginning, the R return the error that "cannot allocate vector of size 28.8Gb". I thought that it was reasonable that my raster layers were too large. Then I changed to another computer that the RAM is 32 Gb, then the R return the error that "cannot allocate vector of size 56 Gb". At last, I changed to another computer which the RAM is 256 Gb, the r showed that it needs another 180Gb. 

I was superised that why R always need more RAM? The prediction function worked well when I used the dataframe to predict the species occupancy at some camera trap stations. Is it because my raster layers are still too large for R to compute?


With kind regards,
Peiyun

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: RAM requirements for prediction
parts:
Hello,
predictions on 30Gb rasters are very unrealistic. In the predict function there are intermediate objects (array) with dimensions: n_cells  x  n_species  x  n_draws.
So a 30Gb raster presumably has billions of cells, multiply that by the number of species and maybe 1000 posterior draws, and you see how memory requirements explode. This also suggests a few ways to reduce memory requirements:
  • work in batches. Two main options:
    • tiling the raster and predicting on each tile
    • use argument batch (it will by default split the input data into batches of 1000 cells) - but it will still require substantial amounts of memory when combining them (and it currently doesn't give a warning about memory requirements, so make sure to monitor memory when trying this)
  • reduce resolution of raster (a good starting point would be to reduce the dimensions to a few hundred rows and columns. Go really low and work your way up from there)
  • use fewer posterior samples (good for testing, but unsuitable for reliable predictions)
I agree that memory requirements are a weak point of this workflow. There are some internal changes I might attempt in the future to alleviate that (e.g. use single precision data type instead of double precision), but that is not implemented yet.
For now I'd recommend drastically reducing the raster size.

Regarding the apparently growing memory requirements on different computers: that is just R reporting where it first runs out of memory. A machine with more memory will succeed where the lesser machine failed, but still runs out of memory at a later point in the code (when even more memory is required).

Best regards,
Jürgen
